pages.intro: Owning a home in Halkidiki is easy while you are here. When you are away for most of the year, someone local has to look after it. Our property management in Halkidiki does that for you: tenants and rent, bills and taxes, maintenance, repairs and regular inspections, all from one team that knows the area.
pages.body:
What our property management includes

You choose what we take over. The full service covers:

  • Tenants: marketing of the property, showings, tenant screening and the lease agreement.
  • Money: rent collection, and the bills and taxes of the property paid on your behalf.
  • Upkeep: maintenance and repairs, carried out when they are needed.
  • Inspections: regular visits to check the state of the property.

Who it is for

Property management suits three kinds of owners in Halkidiki:

  • Owners who live abroad: the house stays closed for months and needs someone to check it, pay its bills and deal with problems.
  • Owners who rent out: a long-term tenant brings an income, but also questions, repairs and rent to collect.
  • New buyers: you have just bought through us and want the home ready, maintained and, if you wish, rented from the first season.

The service is the same team that helped you buy, so the property, its papers and its history are already known to us.

Tenants and rent collection

We advertise the property, show it to interested tenants and check them before anything is signed. We prepare the lease agreement with you and stay the tenants' contact for everyday questions, so they do not call you abroad. The rent is collected on your behalf. When a tenant leaves, we check the property, arrange what needs fixing and look for the next tenant, so that the home does not stay empty longer than needed.

Bills and taxes paid on time

A property in Greece comes with regular payments: electricity, water, the municipal charges and the annual property tax. We pay them for you, so nothing is missed while you are away. Late payments in Greece bring surcharges, and an unpaid bill can mean a supply is cut off just before you arrive; a local contact who pays on time avoids both.

Maintenance, repairs and inspections

We visit the property regularly and look for problems before they grow: humidity, leaks, the garden, the pool, the equipment. When something needs repair, we arrange it and follow the work until it is done. Before a season, we can open the house, air it, check the water, the electricity and the air conditioning, so it is ready when you or your guests arrive; after it, we close it again.

Managing your home while you live abroad

Most of our owners live outside Greece. You agree with us what we manage and how you want to be kept informed, and you deal with one contact instead of several local professionals. If you want to rent out the home, it needs an energy certificate; we arrange that too.

How we start

Talk to us about the property: where it is, what it is like and what you want from it, whether that is a rental income or simply a house that is ready when you arrive. We visit it, agree the scope and the terms with you in writing, and then take over.

faq.q: What does property management in Halkidiki include?
faq.a: Tenant search and screening, the lease agreement, rent collection, the bills and taxes of the property, maintenance and repairs, and regular inspections. You choose what we take over.

faq.q: Can you manage my property while I live abroad?
faq.a: Yes. Most of our owners live outside Greece. We are your local contact and keep you informed the way you agree with us.

faq.q: Do you pay the bills and taxes of my property?

faq.q: Can you find tenants for my property?
faq.a: Yes. We advertise the property, show it, screen the tenants and prepare the lease agreement with you.

faq.q: How much does property management cost?
faq.a: It depends on the property and on what we take over. The terms are agreed with you in writing before we start.

pages.intro: Every home sold or rented in Greece needs an energy performance certificate, the PEA (Πιστοποιητικό Ενεργειακής Απόδοσης). It shows how much energy the building uses and how it could use less. Our energy inspectors arrange the whole PEA for your property in Halkidiki: the documents, the visit and the certificate.
pages.body:
What the PEA is

The PEA is the energy performance certificate of a building in Greece, required by the Buildings' Energy Efficiency Regulation (K.En.A.K.). It records the current energy state of the building, places it in an energy class and proposes ways to improve its performance.

When you need a PEA

A PEA must accompany every sale and every lease of a building or part of a building with a floor area over 50 m². It accompanies the sale contract, and a lease needs it as well. If you plan to sell or rent out, order it early, so that it does not hold up the contract.

How a PEA is issued

A registered energy inspector issues the PEA:

  • Documents: the inspector collects the plans and papers of the property.
  • Visit: the inspector checks the building on site: walls, windows, heating, cooling and hot water.
  • Report: the building is placed in its energy class, with recommendations to improve it.

What the inspector needs from you

Very little. The inspector collects the necessary documents of the property, checks the space on site and prepares the report; our inspectors handle the entire document collection for you. What we need from you is the address of the property, access to it for the visit and the date by which you need the certificate. When you live abroad, we arrange the access and keep you informed until the PEA is issued.

Energy classes and how long a PEA is valid

There are eight energy classes, from A+, the most efficient, to G. A PEA is valid for ten years, and it must be revised earlier if the energy state of the building changes substantially, for example after a renovation. The report does not only give the class: it also proposes methods to improve the energy performance of the building, which you can use when you plan works or when you talk to a buyer.

Why the energy class matters when you sell

The energy class appears in the listing and in the contract, and buyers read it. A better class means lower running costs for heating and cooling, which matters to buyers who will live in the home all year. The recommendations in the PEA also show what a buyer could improve, for example insulation, windows or a heat pump. Knowing the class before you set the price helps you answer these questions with confidence.

We arrange your PEA

Our inspectors handle the whole process for your property in Halkidiki, from the documents to the certificate, also while you live abroad. Tell us where the property is and when you need the certificate.

faq.q: Do I need a PEA to sell my house in Greece?
faq.a: Yes. A sale of a building or part of a building over 50 m² must be accompanied by an energy performance certificate. Our inspectors arrange it for you.

faq.q: Do I need a PEA to rent out my home?
faq.a: Yes. A lease of a building or part of a building over 50 m² needs a PEA too.
A registered energy inspector, after collecting the documents of the property and checking the building on site.

faq.q: How long is a PEA valid?
faq.a: Ten years. It must be renewed earlier if the energy state of the building changes substantially, for example after a renovation.

faq.q: How much does a PEA cost?
faq.a: It depends on the property. Our inspectors handle the documents, the checks and the preparation of the PEA at competitive prices. Tell us where it is and what it is like, and we send you an offer.
